At 336 the manuscripts have a corrupt reading, which in majuscules would be: TOICINAYTOY⟦1⟧IAIC⟦2⟧ACWCI(N)MATAIOI; from this one can make ⟦3⟧ (but also Schol. ⟦4⟧) ⟦5⟧ (Turneb.) ⟦6⟧, or even more easily ⟦7⟧. ⟦8⟧., after ⟦9⟧ ⟦10⟧. ⟦11⟧ is admittedly said more of sufferings than of deeds, and so stands ⟦12⟧ ⟦13⟧ of the murdered man; thus Weil ⟦14⟧, whereby however neither ⟦15⟧ in this sense is properly attested, nor ⟦16⟧ i.e. ⟦17⟧ is possible at all. The difficulty of ⟦18⟧ becomes less if at least the criminal is the subject, who in a blinded and reckless sense (cf. ⟦19⟧ ⟦20⟧, ⟦21⟧ ⟦22⟧, Abresch) commits the crimes that, so to speak, come his way, without hesitation, and so I have preferred ⟦23⟧.
those who with their own deeds
the oozing of blood in time comes together
he falls in with this murder
those who trample him with their own deeds

⟦1⟧ namely ⟦2⟧ or (Schol.) ⟦3⟧; cf. on this transition to the singular above on 313 ff., to which passage Wecklein compares ⟦4⟧ B: ⟦5⟧ . . ⟦6⟧, ⟦7⟧. ⟦8⟧ is a powerfully effective litotes; precisely the half-veiled expression terrifies. Then the fearful refrain is repeated, to bind the criminal all the more firmly.
until he goes under the earth
for no one punishes those who do wrong

Further development of the thought in the antistrophe ⟦1⟧, also in the direction that they are now separated from the gods precisely by their office; to the office they return in the refrain (strophe ⟦2⟧).
